meta.status: DESIGN ONLY — no migration has been applied, no ledger row written, no DDL executed anywhere
meta.orderingChallenge: The naive order (baseline → reference → identity → competitions → pools → financial → matches → predictions → audit → outbox → reporting → backfill → dual-read → server-mediated writes → cutover → freeze → removal) is UNSAFE in five specific ways, each corrected below and each enforced by an executable ordering invariant in scripts/db/validate_migration_phases.mjs. Encoding the corrections as checks rather than prose is deliberate: a prose ordering argument does not survive the next person who finds it convenient to reorder.

orderingCorrections.naive: audit tables created at phase 9, after the financial backfill
orderingCorrections.corrected: audit infrastructure moves to M4, before ANY backfill
orderingCorrections.why: the backfill is the largest data movement in the programme. Creating the audit tables after it means that movement is the one operation with no trail. If a backfill mis-attributes a payment, there is then no record of what it did.

orderingCorrections.naive: server-mediated writes at phase 14, after dual-read
orderingCorrections.corrected: write-through to the relational tables (M11) precedes dual-read comparison (M12)
orderingCorrections.why: dual-read compares JSON against relational. If the app is still writing only to the JSON document, the relational copy is stale from the moment the backfill ends, and every comparison reports a difference that is an artefact of the method rather than a defect. You cannot validate parity against a moving target.

orderingCorrections.naive: reporting views at phase 11, before backfill and cutover
orderingCorrections.corrected: reporting views and matviews move to M15, after cutover
orderingCorrections.why: a materialized view built over a partially backfilled table returns confident, wrong numbers. Worse, it caches them. Reporting must never be the first consumer of unvalidated data.

orderingCorrections.naive: legacy freeze at phase 16, after cutover
orderingCorrections.corrected: a read-only freeze window (M13) precedes final parity validation and cutover (M14)
orderingCorrections.why: parity cannot be proven while the source is mutating. Without a freeze the final comparison is against a document that changed between the two reads, so a genuine mismatch and a concurrent write are indistinguishable.

orderingCorrections.corrected: backfill is decomposed per entity (M8–M10), ordered by FK dependency, each idempotent, restartable and independently validated
orderingCorrections.why: a single backfill phase is a single point of failure with no partial-success state. Halfway through, there is no way to answer 'what is done?' — so the only recovery is to start over, and starting over is only safe if each step was idempotent anyway. Making that explicit costs nothing and removes the all-or-nothing risk.

orderingCorrections.naive: identity de-duplication treated as part of the identity migration
orderingCorrections.corrected: the identity backfill produces ZERO merges (M5); merging is a separate, operator-driven, post-cutover activity (M17)
orderingCorrections.why: a migration that merges identities makes an irreversible money-affecting decision inside an automated batch, at the exact moment nobody is watching individual rows. Every merge requires an operator confirmation (Workstream C), and a migration cannot supply one.

phases.name: baseline_adoption
phases.objects: none — records the existing production schema as the migration baseline
phases.validation: the baseline reference file's digest matches a fresh schema dump; acceptance_checks.mjs EXPECTED_STRUCTURE matches live (7 tables, 3 enums, 1 function, 6 policies, 7 PK, 17 FK, 1 unique index, 8 indexes, 0 user triggers, 7 RLS enabled, 0 forced)
phases.rollback: n/a — no change to roll back
phases.notes: BLOCKED on an operator decision about how the baseline is registered in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations. The two candidate migration-repair calls are NOT authorized, and the previously discussed 'Option E' is de-authorized pending a full restatement of its definition and consequences. Everything from M1 onward is designed to be independent of how M0 is finally recorded, so this blocker does not block the design.

phases.name: schema_and_reference_entities
phases.objects: bolao and audit schemas; competitions, competition_editions, competition_edition_phases; enum types
phases.dataMovement: none — reference rows are inserted, not moved
phases.backfill: insert the known competitions and editions (Copa do Mundo 2026, Brasileirão 2026, Copa do Brasil 2026) and their phases
phases.compatibility: additive only; the legacy app does not read these tables
phases.validation: phase ordinals contiguous per edition (DQ-CP-01); every edition resolves to a competition
phases.rollback: DROP the new schema; no legacy object touched
phases.lockBehavior: CREATE TABLE takes no lock on existing objects
phases.notes: Reference data is small, hand-authored and reviewable. It must NOT be derived from bolao_state, which contains no competition entity at all.

phases.name: identity_tables
phases.validation: self-reference CHECKs present (canonical_participant_id <> participant_id; surviving <> merged)
phases.rollback: DROP TABLE; nothing references them yet
phases.notes: Created before pools and financial because both reference participant_id. Tables first, data later (M5): separating DDL from DML keeps each phase's rollback trivial.

phases.name: pool_and_entry_tables
phases.backfill: pool rows and one in-force fee schedule row per pool
phases.validation: exactly one fee schedule in force per pool (DQ-FN-08); expected_fee_amount is a snapshot column, not a lookup
phases.notes: The fee is a property of the pool rule; pool_entries snapshots it at entry time so a later price change cannot retroactively alter an existing entry's settlement.

phases.name: audit_and_outbox_infrastructure
phases.validation: audit rows immutable after insert except the redactable sidecar; hash-chain columns present
phases.notes: MOVED EARLY (OC-1). Every backfill from M5 onward writes audit events, so the audit tables must exist before the first row moves. Creating them after the backfill would leave the largest data movement in the programme as the only unaudited one.

phases.name: identity_backfill_zero_merges
phases.backfill: one participant per distinct (normalised email, else normalised name). Idempotent on that key. ZERO merges.
phases.validation: PAR-04/PAR-05 (no identity split, no orphan participant); DQ-ID-01 reports duplicate CANDIDATES without acting
phases.rollback: DELETE FROM participants WHERE created_by = 'backfill:M5' — safe because nothing references them yet
phases.lockBehavior: bulk INSERT; row locks only on new rows
phases.notes: ZERO merges by design (OC-6). Duplicate candidates are recorded for operator review in M17. A migration cannot supply the operator confirmation that Workstream C requires for a merge, and an automated merge here would make an irreversible money-affecting decision at the moment nobody is watching individual rows.

phases.name: financial_tables
phases.validation: no ON DELETE CASCADE on any money-bearing FK; every MONETARY_AMOUNT has a CURRENCY_CODE companion; no currency column has a default
phases.notes: No stored settlement column exists, by design. Settlement is derived from payment_allocations; a stored flag would be a second source of truth for money.

phases.name: competition_fact_tables
phases.objects: matches, ties, match_results, predictions, ranking_snapshots, sync_state
phases.validation: at most one official current result per match (DQ-PR-04); predictions have exactly one subject
phases.notes: predictions exists as a table from here, but picks stay in pool_entries.picks jsonb until M16. Decomposing picks changes the scoring input path and is deliberately the very last data change.

phases.name: backfill_entries
phases.backfill: idempotent on pool_entry_id (the client uuid is kept as-is, already a stable surrogate); restartable; batched
phases.validation: PAR-01/PAR-02/PAR-03 (count, id set, tombstones); PAR-12 (picks byte-identical); PAR-13 (fee explicit)
phases.rollback: DELETE by pool_id — no legacy row touched
phases.lockBehavior: bulk INSERT into a new table; no lock on anything the app reads
phases.notes: Decomposed per entity (OC-5). expected_fee_amount is passed in explicitly, never inferred: B-08 established entryFee=5 as authoritative for current pools and U1 ratified USD, but a historical pool with an unknown fee stays UNKNOWN.

phases.name: backfill_payments_asserted_only
phases.dataMovement: bolao_state.paid{entryId→true} → payments with amount NULL and legacy_asserted
phases.backfill: one asserted payment per paid=true entry; NO payment_allocations rows; idempotent on (asserted_for_pool_entry_id)
phases.validation: PAR-06 (one assertion per flag, no invented amount), PAR-07 (no fabricated allocation), PAR-14/PAR-15 (payer attribution and self-payment)
phases.notes: The highest-risk backfill in the programme, because it is the one that touches money. The legacy `paid` boolean carries no amount, date, method, reference or actor (D-1), so nothing may be invented: settlement for these entries is LEGACY_ASSERTED, an honest fifth state rather than a fabricated number. Third-party payers known only by free-text name stay UNKNOWN-1.

phases.name: backfill_results_audit_and_sync
phases.dataMovement: results{} → match_results; auditLog[] → audit.audit_events (PII stripped); lastSync → sync_state
phases.backfill: idempotent on match_id and on (occurred_at, action) respectively; audit hash chain computed in document order
phases.validation: PAR-08 (line count), PAR-09 (no free-text detail carried), PAR-10 (order preserved), PAR-11 (result keys), DQ-AU-01/02
phases.rollback: DELETE by source marker; the audit chain is recomputed rather than patched
phases.notes: auditLog[].detail is deliberately dropped (B1/ADR-008): carrying free text across would reintroduce exactly the PII the audit model exists to keep out. Ordering must be preserved or the hash chain is meaningless.

phases.name: write_through_via_server_mediated_writes
phases.objects: Edge Function write endpoints (Workstream S contracts); RLS policies for the service role (Workstream R)
phases.dataMovement: new writes land in BOTH the legacy jsonb document and the relational tables, in one transaction where possible
phases.compatibility: the legacy app keeps working unchanged; new writes are additionally captured relationally
phases.validation: every write contract produces an audit event and an outbox event; idempotency keys enforced
phases.rollback: disable the write-through flag; the legacy document remains authoritative and complete
phases.appDependency: app must call the new endpoints; old clients still writing directly to the document are the reason M12 measures divergence rather than assuming zero
phases.notes: MOVED BEFORE dual-read (OC-2). Without write-through, the relational copy is stale from the instant M10 finishes, so every dual-read comparison reports method artefacts instead of defects. Dual-WRITE is justified here specifically and only here: it is the only way to hold two representations comparable during a cutover, and it is removed at M16.

phases.name: dual_read_comparison
phases.dataMovement: none; reads both representations and records differences
phases.compatibility: read-only; the legacy document remains authoritative
phases.validation: json_parity.mjs coverage + 15 invariants + round-trip against live pairs; zero UNAUTHORISED differences required for N consecutive runs
phases.notes: The exit criterion is zero unauthorised differences, not zero differences: paid, deletedIds, auditLog[].detail and siteVersion differ BY DESIGN, each citing the decision authorising it. 'The round trip differs' is not actionable; 'it differs in a way nobody authorised' is.

phases.name: legacy_freeze_window
phases.dataMovement: none — writes to the legacy document are rejected for the duration
phases.backfill: a final catch-up pass for anything written between the last dual-read run and the freeze
phases.compatibility: the app is read-only for the window; entries cannot be created or edited
phases.validation: post-freeze parity run must show zero unauthorised differences on a static source
phases.rollback: lift the freeze; nothing has changed structurally
phases.appDependency: the UI must show an explicit read-only state, not fail silently
phases.lockBehavior: application-level, not database-level; no table lock is taken
phases.notes: MOVED BEFORE cutover (OC-4). Parity cannot be proven against a mutating source: without the freeze, a genuine mismatch and a concurrent write look identical. The window must be scheduled outside a match/cutoff period — a freeze during a prediction deadline would deny entries and directly affect who can play.

phases.name: cutover
phases.dataMovement: authority moves: the relational tables become the source of truth; the legacy document becomes a shadow copy
phases.compatibility: the app reads relationally; the document is still written for one release as a rollback path
phases.validation: post-cutover smoke: create an entry, submit a prediction, record a payment, read every report, verify the audit chain
phases.rollback: flip the authority flag back; the document is still current because it is still being written
phases.appDependency: a release that reads relationally must be deployed and confirmed healthy first
phases.lockBehavior: none — a configuration flip, not a DDL change
phases.notes: The rollback path is what makes this survivable: for one release the legacy document is still maintained, so reverting is a flag flip rather than a restore. That is the entire reason M16 is a separate phase.

phases.name: reporting_layer
phases.objects: views and materialized views from model/reports.json; the index set from INDEX_STRATEGY.md
phases.validation: each report returns rows consistent with the equivalent computation in financial.mjs; R-15 must agree exactly with poolReconciliation()
phases.rollback: DROP VIEW / DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW; no base data affected
phases.lockBehavior: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY for every index; a plain CREATE INDEX would block writes for the duration
phases.notes: MOVED AFTER cutover (OC-3). A matview over a partially backfilled table returns confident, wrong numbers and then caches them. Reporting must never be the first consumer of unvalidated data.

phases.name: legacy_write_removal_and_picks_decomposition
phases.dataMovement: picks jsonb → predictions rows; legacy document writes stop
phases.backfill: one prediction per (entry, match) from the preserved picks blob; idempotent
phases.compatibility: BREAKING for any client still writing the document; requires the stale-session handling in the zero-downtime strategy
phases.validation: Workstream N scoring parity — every score, rank and tie identical before and after, computed by the app's own scoring logic on both representations
phases.rollback: predictions rows can be dropped; picks jsonb is RETAINED as the fallback until N passes on production-shaped data
phases.appDependency: all clients must be on a release that neither reads nor writes the legacy document
phases.lockBehavior: bulk INSERT into predictions; picks column is not dropped in this phase
phases.notes: Deliberately last, because it is the only phase that changes the scoring input path. picks is not dropped here — keeping the blob costs storage and removes the need to be right the first time. Dropping it is a later, separate decision once N has passed repeatedly.

phases.name: post_cutover_operator_identity_review
phases.backfill: none — this is not a batch
phases.validation: every merge carries {operatorId, reason}; DQ-ID-02/03/04/05 clean afterwards; reversibility exercised at least once on a synthetic pair before touching a real one
phases.rollback: reverseMerge per link, restoring prior_state exactly
phases.appDependency: an operator UI for the candidate queue
phases.notes: Separate from the migration by design (OC-6). Merges move money attribution and require a human decision per pair; a migration cannot supply one. This phase has no completion date — it is ongoing operational work, and treating it as a migration step would create pressure to bulk-approve.

orderingInvariants.rule: audit_and_outbox_infrastructure must precede every phase whose name starts with backfill_
at least three distinct backfill_ phases must exist
the identity backfill phase must declare zero merges, and no phase before post_cutover_operator_identity_review may perform a merge
every destructive phase must have a rollback that is not 'none'
scoring_parity validation must be named by the phase that decomposes picks
